correctness.rationale: For paths of one or two edges let s=p/2, A=1−s, q=1−s². Complementing both indicators preserves covariance; the common failure marginal is Aq^(n−2). Each external vertex contributes a factor independent of the others and of endpoint edges: 1−2s² for reverse/chain (opposite arc demands), 1−2s²+s³ for a fork (one shared arc), q² for disjoint requests. Endpoint reverse failure requires no edge; a fork needs just its two direct failures. For the chain, conditioning on the two direct failures makes the two interior witnesses have probabilities s²/A each and overlap s³/A², giving endpoint factor A²−2As²+s³. For the disjoint case the two direct failures leave four candidate two-step paths; two witness pairs conflict, two have probability s³ and two have probability s⁴, and every triple contains a conflicting pair. Its endpoint factor is A²(1−4s²+2s³+2s⁴). The chain deficit relative to A²q² is s³[1−2s+s(1−s)²]>0; the disjoint conditional surplus relative to q⁴ is s³[2(1−2s)+s³(4−s²)]>0. Reverse strictness follows from 1−2s<A², and fork strictness already holds on three endpoints (q<1). These checks cover the minimum vertex counts and p=1; p=0 is degenerate and identical requests have positive variance for p>0. Independently counted all orientations/absences for n=2,3,4,5 using adjacency bit sets and integer counts by number of edges, and compared joint laws and signs at p=0,1/9,1/2,5/7,1: python /workspace/branches/twohop_replay.py (3, 27, 729, 59049 configurations respectively). This is corroboration, not the all-order argument. Theorem 2.1 of Alm–Janson–Linusson establishes the stated unrestricted asymptotic contrast, including fixed p=1.
